clue.text: Prosaic practical way to earn one's daily bread

definitions.text: practical way to earn one's daily bread
definitions.meaning: read as a phrase: put in a shift of labour every day to make a living

explanation.surface: A dull but sensible description of how ordinary people make their living.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses rest on ordinary routine labour: the adjective means commonplace, and the split phrase describes a day spent at a job.

definitions.note: the adjective stands in loosely for a Canadian province itself, a typical older Times liberty

indicators.note: a sort of oration is a version of it, so its letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Describes a speech delivered in a rustic, small-town manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges the letters of ORATION. ONTARIO is a province of Canada, hence 'Provincial'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the provinces of Canada, so something from there is provincial.

clue.text: Thrill to George Bernard's fantastic creation

parts.note: a thrill is a kick, as in doing it for kicks
George Bernard Shaw, the playwright, so his surname with a possessive

explanation.surface: Excitement at the playwright's imaginative new play.
explanation.walkthrough: A kickshaw is a fancy, insubstantial dish or a trinket; the word comes from French quelque chose.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a fancy trifle or elaborate dainty dish, something whimsical and showy rather than substantial.

clue.text: Composer, God willing, comes upon king hidden in tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: DV is short for Deo volente, Latin for God willing

indicators.note: the king is concealed inside the tree, so one letter goes into the other word

parts.note: an oak is a tree
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A composer, if God permits, stumbles on a monarch concealed in an oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes upon' places DV above the rest; 'hidden in' puts R inside OAK to make ORAK. Dvorak was the Czech composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was a Czech composer, of the New World Symphony.

parts.note: not a magazine subscription but the formula one writes beneath a letter when corresponding

explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard sign-off at the foot of a formal letter, and to subscribe originally meant to write one's name underneath.

indicators.note: the word me goes inside another word here, a container

parts.note: hit hard means hit severely

explanation.surface: Someone complains of being badly hurt internally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts ME within HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: To be harmed is to be injured or damaged.

parts.note: a cheerful holiday falling midway through a school session

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain half-term is a short holiday of about a week midway through each school term.
explanation.definitionFit: British schools take a short holiday in the middle of each session, a welcome rest from lessons.

clue.text: Prime exponent of some art form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of some art are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: The leading practitioner of a particular kind of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like part of 'art form' but it is the anagram signal on SOME ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially a great conductor or musician, its foremost exponent.

parts.note: a naval vessel named after the Hindu god whose role is to destroy

explanation.walkthrough: HMS marks a Royal Navy ship; Siva is known as the Destroyer, so a ship of that name is doubly a warship of this class.
explanation.definitionFit: Siva (Shiva) is the destroying god of the Hindu trinity, and a ship with HMS before its name would be a warship.

clue.text: Cuts about half a coat — a house-coat

indicators.note: turned about, so the word cuts is read backwards
the first half of the word coat is taken

explanation.surface: Trimming a dressing gown down to half its length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns CUTS to STUC; 'half' takes CO from 'coat'. 'house-coat' is not a dressing gown but a coat of plaster on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is plaster rendering applied as an outer coating to the walls of buildings.

clue.text: No good looks single us out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of single us are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains that being unattractive gets them singled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SINGLE US.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is the lack of attractive features, the opposite of beauty.

clue.text: Lock holding well might prevent this

definitions.text: Lock holding well might prevent this

indicators.note: the lock of hair holds another word inside it, a container

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: A door lock that holds firm would keep out intruders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts SPA inside TRESS after its third letter. Read whole, a lock that holds well stops unlawful entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Trespass is unlawful entry onto property, exactly what a secure lock is meant to stop.

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, and there are two of them
the second tar

explanation.surface: Asks where a condiment came from, answered by a pair of seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartar sauce, a mayonnaise relish with capers, is served with fish.

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy
la is a French word for the
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Lists rivers in the far north, one of them in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar describes the regions round the poles, so the Arctic is one example.

clue.text: Fancy supply of paper sent by tube

parts.note: piped means conveyed through a pipe or tube
a ream is a quantity of paper, 480 or 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Wondering about paper delivered through a pneumatic tube system.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts appear in the clue in reverse of their order in the answer; 'Fancy' is a noun, a whimsical notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy here is an unrealistic hope or idle fantasy.

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the slang sum, a container

parts.note: pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
a trim is a light haircut

explanation.surface: A small sum cut from a legacy of twenty-five pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A TRIM inside PONY, after its P. PONY is British slang for £25.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrimony is property handed down from one's father or ancestors, a legacy.

clue.text: Don't finish complaint, or it could be awkward

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for complaint is left off

parts.note: a malady is a complaint or illness

indicators.note: or it could be rearranged into another arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: Advice to someone griping not to finish, or it would be embarrassing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't finish' cuts MALADY to MALAD; 'could be' rearranges OR IT to ROIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy or lacking skill, the opposite of adroit.

parts.note: not God creating the world, but the maker of a famous carved stone work of art titled Genesis

explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to God as the creator in the book of Genesis, but Genesis is also a famous statue by Jacob Epstein.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein carved the stone figure Genesis, so its creator was one who carves statues.

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language
cute means attractive and pleasing

explanation.surface: Advice to rehearse composition and charm.
explanation.walkthrough: To prosecute can mean to carry on or practise a trade or activity, not only to take to court.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense it means to pursue or carry on an activity, such as a trade.

definitions.meaning: relating to the old Turkish empire
a low upholstered seat or footstool

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Turkish empire of Osman's line, and the noun is a padded stool without a back.

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
King Lear, Shakespeare's monarch

explanation.surface: A command to a monarch to leap around.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a fence is to jump over it cleanly.

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a round is a ring or circle

explanation.surface: A silver band resting at the bottom of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship aground has its hull resting on the seabed, stuck in shallow water.

definitions.meaning: sandalwood, the fragrant timber, is called by this short name
an open shoe held on by straps

explanation.definitionFit: Both are senses of one spelling: a fragrant tropical timber, and a strapped open shoe.

clue.text: In particular, imitate the farmer's wife

definitions.meaning: a particular, as a noun, is a single item or point
in the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cuts off the tails of three blind mice

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link. In the rhyme Three Blind Mice the farmer's wife cut off their tails with a carving knife, so to imitate her is to de-tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is an individual point or item; and copying the rhyme's knife-wielding wife means removing tails.

parts.note: a woman named after a region of Belgium, as in Defoe's novel title

explanation.walkthrough: Moll Flanders is the heroine of Daniel Defoe's 1722 novel; the region is the Dutch-speaking north of Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's heroine Moll bears the name of the region straddling Belgium and France, so a Belgian Moll suggests her surname.

clue.text: Give me back crackers and cheese

indicators.note: the word me is given back, read in reverse

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad, mental

explanation.surface: A request at the table for biscuits and some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM. 'crackers' is not the biscuits but slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with large holes.

clue.text: A number take sport with this air target

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
in biology a sport is a mutant plant or animal, also called a rogue

explanation.surface: Players are told to have fun with this aerial target.
explanation.walkthrough: A sport, in gardening and biology, is an individual that departs from type, also called a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A drogue is a fabric sleeve towed behind an aircraft as a target for gunnery practice.

indicators.note: translating changes words into another form, so the letters of German are rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolboy's cheat sheet for German homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges GERMAN. 'a crib' is not a cheat's translation but a feeding trough, as in the Nativity.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a feeding trough for animals, which is also called a crib.

clue.text: 'At the present time, you heartlessly let mongrel die

indicators.note: without its heart, the middle letter of the word you is removed
a mongrel is a mixed breed, so the letters of die are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone callously allows a stray dog to die, at this very moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' cuts YOU to YU; 'mongrel' rearranges DIE to IDE. 'present' means gifts: Christmas is the time of presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the Christmas season, when gifts are given.
